Symptoms Signs Your Automatic Gearbox Needs Attention Automatic gearboxes give you warning signs - but they're different from manuals. Don't ignore them. Harsh or jerky shifting Valve body issue, worn clutch packs, low fluid ⚠️ Get checked - progressive wear Slipping between gears Worn clutch packs, low fluid pressure, fluid contamination ⚠️ Get checked - could lead to complete failure Delayed engagement (D or R) Low fluid, worn pump, solenoid issue, valve body wear ⚠️ Get checked - early indicator of serious issues Transmission overheating Low fluid, clogged cooler, internal wear 🔴 Get checked immediately - heat destroys automatics Transmission warning light Internal fault - fluid temp, solenoid, sensor, speed sensor 🔴 Get checked - driving could cause catastrophic damage Whining or humming noise Worn bearings, low fluid, pump wear ⚠️ Get checked - progressive wear Burning smell Overheated fluid - clutch packs slipping 🔴 Stop driving - possible fire risk Leaking fluid (red/brown) Seals worn, damaged casing, cooler line leak ⚠️ Get checked - low fluid causes internal wear Rough idle in gear Torque converter issue, engine mount wear ⚠️ Get checked - could be converter or mounts No drive in any gear Complete internal failure, pump failure, valve body failure 🔴 Do not drive - immediate replacement needed When to Stop Driving Immediately Complete loss of drive Major internal failure - driving is impossible. Transmission warning light Internal fault - driving could destroy the gearbox. Burning smell Fluid overheating - clutch packs are slipping. Loud grinding / clunking Internal damage - driving could cause catastrophic failure. "Automatic gearboxes give you more warning than manuals - but the warning signs are different. Why it costs more Why Automatic Costs More - The Complexity Factor Automatic gearboxes are significantly more complex than manuals, which drives up cost. Labour rates vary by region. Valve body note The Valve Body / Mechatronic Note - Not Always Full Replacement Many automatic gearbox issues are valve body or mechatronic unit failures - and these can often be repaired rather than replaced. 🔧 What Is the Valve Body / Mechatronic Unit? Valve Body - Controls fluid flow to clutch packs. Like the "brain" of the gearbox. Failure signs: harsh shifting, delayed engagement, slipping. Mechatronic Unit - Integrated valve body + electronics (common in DSG/DCT). Failure signs: same as above + warning lights, limp mode. Solenoids - Electrically controlled valves within the valve body. Failure signs: individual gear issues, delayed engagement. When Valve Body Repair Makes Sense Scenario Valve Body Repair Cost [EM-QUOTE] Full Replacement Cost [EM-QUOTE] Saving Harsh shifting, no internal damage £400-£1,000 £2,000-£5,000 £1,000-£4,000 Delayed engagement, no slipping £400-£1,200 £2,000-£5,000 £800-£3,800 Warning light, code points to solenoid £300-£800 £2,000-£5,000 £1,200-£4,200 [EM-QUOTE] based on supplier data. Valve body repair can save thousands. "About 40% of automatic gearbox 'failures' we see are actually valve body or mechatronic issues - not full gearbox failures. The customer thinks they need a new gearbox, but a £500-£1,000 valve body repair solves the problem. Always get a proper diagnostic before assuming the worst." - UK Gearbox Specialist Interview #11 [EM-INTERVIEW] Important: If the valve body has failed due to internal debris (from worn clutch packs), the gearbox itself may also be damaged. Always get a full diagnostic before deciding on valve body repair vs full replacement. Get automatic gearbox replacement quotes now → Compare now Frequently asked questions Automatic Gearbox FAQs How much does automatic gearbox replacement cost? − Torque converter automatic £1,000-£4,000 , CVT £1,200-£5,000 , DSG/DCT £1,500-£7,000 . Prices vary by gearbox type, condition, and vehicle. What's the difference between torque converter, CVT, and DSG? + Torque converter - traditional auto, smooth, uses fluid coupling. CVT - uses pulleys and belts, seamless ratio changes. DSG/DCT - dual-clutch, fast shifts, sporty. Can a valve body issue be repaired without replacing the whole gearbox? + Yes - many automatic gearbox issues (harsh shifting, delayed engagement) are valve body or mechatronic issues. Repair costs £400-£1,200 - far less than full replacement. What are the signs of automatic gearbox failure? + Harsh shifting, slipping between gears, delayed engagement, transmission overheating, transmission warning light, whining noise, burning smell, leaking fluid. How long does automatic gearbox replacement take? + Labour typically takes 8-15 hours (1-3 days) . Additional time for sourcing the gearbox. Allow 3-7 days for the complete process. What warranty comes with an automatic gearbox replacement? + Used: 3-6 months. Reconditioned: 6-24 months. New: 12-24 months. Always check the specific terms with your supplier. Is automatic gearbox replacement more expensive than manual? + Yes - automatic gearboxes are more complex, have more components, and require more labour. Typical automatic replacement costs £1,000-£5,000 vs manual £500-£3,000 . Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer? + Gearbox replacement doesn't require DVLA notification. You should check with your insurer - some policies require notification of major mechanical changes. Ready to find your automatic gearbox replacement? The following insights are drawn from interviews with UK gearbox specialists [EM-INTERVIEW] .

"A customer came in with a BMW 5 Series - harsh shifting, delayed engagement. The main dealer quoted £4,000 for a new gearbox. We diagnosed it as a valve body issue. £800 later, the gearbox was shifting like new. That's the difference a proper diagnostic makes."

"DSG gearboxes are brilliant when they work - and expensive when they don't. The mechatronic unit is the most common failure point. A mechatronic repair or replacement costs £600-£1,500 - far less than a full gearbox replacement. But it needs specialist knowledge."

"CVT gearboxes are often neglected. The fluid needs changing every 60,000-80,000 miles. If you don't, the belt and pulleys wear, and the gearbox fails. A fluid change is £200-£400. A full CVT replacement is £2,000-£4,000."

blocks.question: How much does automatic gearbox replacement cost? −
blocks.answer: Torque converter automatic £1,000-£4,000 , CVT £1,200-£5,000 , DSG/DCT £1,500-£7,000 . Prices vary by gearbox type, condition, and vehicle.

blocks.question: What's the difference between torque converter, CVT, and DSG? +
blocks.answer: Torque converter - traditional auto, smooth, uses fluid coupling. CVT - uses pulleys and belts, seamless ratio changes. DSG/DCT - dual-clutch, fast shifts, sporty.

blocks.question: Can a valve body issue be repaired without replacing the whole gearbox? +
blocks.answer: Yes - many automatic gearbox issues (harsh shifting, delayed engagement) are valve body or mechatronic issues. Repair costs £400-£1,200 - far less than full replacement.

blocks.question: What are the signs of automatic gearbox failure? +
blocks.answer: Harsh shifting, slipping between gears, delayed engagement, transmission overheating, transmission warning light, whining noise, burning smell, leaking fluid.

blocks.question: How long does automatic gearbox replacement take? +
blocks.answer: Labour typically takes 8-15 hours (1-3 days) . Additional time for sourcing the gearbox. Allow 3-7 days for the complete process.

blocks.question: What warranty comes with an automatic gearbox replacement? +
blocks.answer: Used: 3-6 months. Reconditioned: 6-24 months. New: 12-24 months. Always check the specific terms with your supplier.

blocks.question: Is automatic gearbox replacement more expensive than manual? +
blocks.answer: Yes - automatic gearboxes are more complex, have more components, and require more labour. Typical automatic replacement costs £1,000-£5,000 vs manual £500-£3,000 .

blocks.question: Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer? +
blocks.answer: Gearbox replacement doesn't require DVLA notification. You should check with your insurer - some policies require notification of major mechanical changes.
